title: Prefix key entropy mapping and safe-apply runbook for TTL & caching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce an operationally safe guidance and automation bundle that recommends prefix cache key designs, models per-prefix hit-rate, suggests TTL ladders, and provides a staged apply + automated rollback runbook for Dedicated and Hosted deployments. The outcome should reduce per-token cost (via higher effective cache hit rate and better batching) without increasing tail latency or causing cache pollution. This ticket bundles: 1) a lightweight hit-rate explainability model (prefix-level telemetry -> hit probability), 2) a TTL ladder generator that proposes conservative to aggressive settings, 3) a prefix entropy mapping tool to find harmful shard/key groupings, and 4) a safe-apply orchestration with dry-run shadowing, canary windows, and automated rollback triggers tied to cost/latency/regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver a documented hit-rate model that explains predicted hit-rate per prefix + confidence band
TTL ladder generator produces 3-tier suggestions (conservative/standard/aggressive) for a given workload and a rationale string
Prefix entropy mapper identifies top-20 high-entropy prefixes and suggests key-normalization transforms
Safe-apply runbook implemented as a CI task + orchestration script with automated abort on regression signals
Playbook validated in staging with two customer-like traffic traces and rollbacks automated on at least one induced regression
PRs (runtime + control-plane) merged and console UI checklist added for operators
tasks: Prototype prefix entropy mapping script and run on last 7 days of prod-sampled telemetry
Build hit-rate explainability model (lightweight GLM + feature importance strings) and vet against sampled traces
Design TTL ladder heuristics and tie to batching sensitivity metadata
Implement canary apply orchestration: dry-run shadow, 1% canary, 5% ramp, full apply
Wire automatic rollback triggers: 99th pct latency increase > 20ms OR token cost increase > 8% OR eval prompt regression > threshold
Create staged operator checklist and alerting playbook in Console
Run two staging experiments and record results in Confluence
notes: Design decision: use a conservative default TTL ladder so first-stage apply has minimal customer-visible regression risk.
We will prefer non-invasive key-normalization transforms (e.g., strip session ids, truncate user-generated suffixes) before aggressive TTL reductions.
Batching sensitivity: TTL changes that reduce KV cache usage may increase per-request token work; the TTL ladder ties into batching profiles to avoid regressive throughput impacts.
Noise tolerance: automated rollback uses smoothed metrics over two 5-minute windows separated by 1 minute to avoid flapping on transient spikes.
